subject: Post-call: inference fit & deployment checklist for NovusPay
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: inference fit & deployment checklist for NovusPay

Hi Tim / Olga —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, below is a concise recap of the production needs you described, the constraints we flagged, and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please reply with any corrections and confirm the priority items we should include in the POC scope.

Key business problem
- Real-time transaction risk scoring (pre-authorization) where decisions must be returned inline with checkout flows.
- Goal: reduce false-positive declines while keeping decision latency imperceptible to end users.

Pain points you called out
- Current vendor adds ~300–600ms to checkout; customer drop-off too high.
- Spiky traffic around payroll cycles: sustained ~150 req/s with peak bursts up to ~800 req/s for ~10–15 minutes.
- Regulatory requirement: logs/audit for model inferences retained for 90 days; keys stored in customer KMS.

Target goals we heard
- P95 inference latency target: ~60ms (transaction-level end-to-end).
- Typical prompt size: 30–80 tokens; average response payload ~40 tokens.
- Throughput: steady-state ~150–200 req/s; burst capacity target ~800 req/s.

Technical constraints / preferences
- Prefer private network options (VPC) due to PCI-sensitivity; willingness to evaluate Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment.
- Plan to use an open LLM backbone (you mentioned Llama3 family) — acceptable to use quantized variants for cost.

Initial topology options (high level)
1) Dedicated GPUs (reserved capacity) in us-west-2 + autoscale for short bursts (recommended for fastest time to production).
2) Private control plane (VPC) on our infra if you require full network isolation; longer lead time for on-prem validation.
3) Hybrid: Dedicated for baseline traffic + fallback to smaller quantized model for excess bursts.

Immediate POC scope recommendations
- Validate P95 <= 60ms for typical prompt/response (40 tokens) under 150 req/s sustained.
- Verify autoscale behavior during 10–15 minute 800 req/s bursts with prefix/KV caching enabled.
- Confirm log delivery to your audit pipeline (S3) and KMS integration.

Attachments (attached to this thread):
- novuspay-slo-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet with test vectors & traffic shape)

Next steps (please confirm):
- Tim: confirm which deployment mode you want us to prioritize for the POC (Dedicated vs Private VPC).
- Olga: share 1 week of anonymized traffic trace and one example prompt set.
- Redwood (Marissa): send a recommended topology with expected GPU sizing and a rough cost estimate.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-1283

Subject: Re: Post-call: inference fit & deployment checklist for NovusPay

Jasmine — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 60ms P95 is what we want end-to-end from request arrival to scoring decision in checkout. If you can demonstrate 60ms with an allowance of +/-10ms for network overhead that would be ideal.
- Traffic shape: sustained ~150 req/s is correct; daily peak windows reach ~800 req/s for ~10–20 minutes. We can reproduce the spike in a controlled fashion for the POC.
- Model family: yes, Llama3-8B variants look promising. We are open to int8 or int4 quantized variants if they retain accuracy.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you include a rough monthly cost ballpark for Dedicated capacity sized to handle the burst profile (just an order-of-magnitude)?
2) For audit/logging, we need sample log format (fields + retention options).

Attachment: sample-traffic-summary.csv (not attached here, will upload to the Drive link)

Happy to run the POC in September — we prefer Sep 12–16.

Best,
Tim

Tim / Jasmine —

Thanks — below are concrete topology and sizing recommendations for the POC based on the traffic you described. I focused on configurations that prioritize P95 latency while keeping GPU counts reasonable.

Quick assumptions (POC):
- Model: redwood-llama3-8b-int8 (provisionally). Average response length: 40 tokens.
- Network: colocated in us-west-2, low-latency VPC peering to NovusPay.
- Caching: KV/prefix caching enabled for repeated prefixes (we should expect ~20–25% token reuse).

Sizing guidance (approximate; will refine after traffic trace):
- Baseline steady-state 150 req/s: 1 x NVIDIA A40 or A100 (80GB) with batching tuned to 4–6; expected P95 ~45–65ms for 40-token responses with int8 weights and cache warm.
- Burst handling to 800 req/s (10–20 minute windows): recommended approach: 3–4 active inference GPUs + 2 extra GPUs available for fast warm-up (autoscale target). That gives effective peak capacity ~700–900 req/s depending on batching and burst density.
- Fallback: a smaller quantized 3B variant for overflow that increases P95 to ~80–120ms but keeps service available and lowers cost.

Performance levers we will tune in POC
- Batch size (tradeoff latency vs throughput) — target 4–8 for best P95 for these short prompts.
- KV cache TTL and prefix cache thresholds to reduce repeated token computation.
- Quantization profile: int8 for primary; int4 candidate if accuracy tests pass.
- Request routing: sticky routing for ongoing sessions to maximize cache hits.

Estimated GPU counts for desired SLOs (POC):
- Minimum for POC baseline: 1 dedicated A100 + 1 autoscale reserve node (test scale-up triggers).
- For production to handle sustained 800 req/s with P95 ~60ms: likely 4–6 A100-class GPUs (final number depends on measured prompt lengths and batch tuning).

Attachments: proposed-topology.png (diagram) — included here.

I can prepare a short runbook for the POC: test vectors, latency targets, traffic replay steps, and validation queries that exercise worst-case prompt shapes. If you approve, I’ll upload the runbook and a one-page sizing matrix to the Drive link Jasmine shared.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
